name: Saint John Eudes
history: A Norman priest and tireless preacher of parish missions who founded a congregation to train priests in seminaries and another to care for women leaving prostitution. He was the first to compose liturgical feasts in honour of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Heart of Mary.
life: John Eudes joined the French Oratory under Cardinal de Bérulle and was ordained in 1625. When plague struck Normandy he nursed the sick, and in one outbreak lived apart, it is said in a large cask in a field, so as not to carry the infection to his brothers. For more than fifty years he preached missions across Normandy and beyond, often with a team of confessors. Convinced that the reform of the Church depended on well-formed priests, he left the Oratory in 1643 and founded the Congregation of Jesus and Mary, the Eudists, to run seminaries. He also founded the Order of Our Lady of Charity for women who wished to leave prostitution, from which the Good Shepherd Sisters later grew. He wrote Masses and Offices for the Heart of Mary and the Heart of Jesus, and kept them in his communities long before the universal Church did. He died at Caen in 1680 and was canonised in 1925.
prayerTo: Saint John Eudes, you loved the Hearts of Jesus and Mary and spent your life for priests, for sinners and for the sick. Pray for seminarians and all who form them, for women caught in exploitation, and for me, that my heart may be made like the heart of Christ. Amen.
penance: Pray today for seminarians and vocations, and support a charity that helps women escape trafficking or exploitation.
meditation: He taught that Christians should continue the life of Jesus in their own lives, as members of His body. In what one thing today could you let Christ live through you?
prayer: O God, Who wondrously enkindled St. John, Your Confessor, to promote the religious veneration of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary, and through him willed to found new religious families in the Church; grant, we beseech You, that we may honor his holy merits and may learn from the example of his virtues. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
